title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 150 (Manner of selection of independent directors)

content.overview: Section 150 provides that an independent director may be selected from a data bank of persons who are eligible and willing to act as independent directors, maintained by any body, institute or association as may be notified by the Central Government. The data bank is a source of candidates; appointment remains governed by sections 149 and 152 and the company’s due diligence on the independence criteria.
content.glance: Independent directors may be selected from a notified data bank of eligible and willing persons; data bank is a source, not an appointment; company must still satisfy s. 149 criteria.
content.study: An independent director may be selected from a data bank containing names, addresses and qualifications of persons who are eligible and willing to act as independent directors, maintained by any body, institute or association as may be notified by the Central Government, in such manner and subject to such conditions as may be prescribed. The responsibility of exercising due diligence before selecting a person from the data bank as an independent director remains with the company. Appointment itself is effected under sections 149 and 152; the data bank does not appoint. Current-law framing: identify proposed independent director; check data-bank selection if used; apply s. 149(6) independence criteria and appointment formalities under s. 152.

sections.heading: Data Bank
sections.body: A notified body maintains a data bank of persons eligible and willing to act as independent directors, with names, addresses and qualifications.

sections.heading: Selection, Not Appointment
sections.body: Selection from the data bank is optional as a source. Appointment remains an act of the company under sections 149 and 152.

sections.heading: Due Diligence
sections.body: The company must exercise due diligence on the independence criteria in section 149(6) before selecting a person from the data bank.

provisions.title: Manner of selection of independent directors

examples.title: Data-bank selection
examples.body: A listed company shortlists an independent-director candidate from the notified data bank and then verifies independence under s. 149(6) before appointment under s. 152.

examples.title: Data bank is not appointment
examples.body: Mere listing in the data bank does not make a person a director. Appointment requires company resolution and statutory formalities.

hypotheticals.question: Does selection from the data bank dispense with independence criteria under s. 149?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. Section 150 is a selection source. The company remains responsible for due diligence on s. 149(6) criteria and for appointment under s. 152.

distinctions.title: Selection of independent directors (s. 150) vs board composition (s. 149)
distinctions.left: Optional data-bank source for independent-director candidates
distinctions.right: Minimum/maximum directors, resident, woman and independent-director requirements

misconceptions.trap: Anyone on the data bank is automatically an independent director of the company.
misconceptions.correction: The data bank is only a source. Appointment and independence criteria under ss. 149 and 152 still apply.

questionsAndAnswers.question: How should a Section 150 problem be analysed?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: I. Identify proposed independent director. II. Note data-bank selection if used. III. Apply s. 149 independence criteria. IV. Confirm appointment under s. 152. V. Conclude.

questionsAndAnswers.question: What should submissions contain?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Data-bank facts if any; due diligence; independence criteria; appointment formalities; precise relief.
